Definition: from G4314 and a derivative of the same as G3730 (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at:--draw to the shore.
BiblicalUsage: Prosormizo means to moor to, to bring a ship to shore. It appears once, when Jesus and the disciples crossed the sea and came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the shore they reached was the place of the next healing: they had hardly landed before the sick were carried to Him.
